vocabulary.definition: A medical condition causing pain and stiffness in joints and muscles.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「風濕病」。年長者常患的關節肌肉疼痛病症。
vocabulary.example: He joked that his joint pain was just a mild case of rheumatism.

vocabulary.definition: Dark or poorly lit; feeling distressed or pessimistic.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞，意為「陰暗的；抑鬱的；陰沉的」。形容天氣或心情沉悶低落。
vocabulary.example: The classroom felt gloomy on rainy Monday mornings.

vocabulary.definition: Unconventional and slightly strange in behavior or appearance.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞/名詞，意為「古怪的；怪異的；行為特立獨行的人」。常用於形容天才特別的習性。
vocabulary.example: People thought the scientist was eccentric because he never wore socks.

vocabulary.definition: Rightfully earned or merited because of actions or qualities.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞/動詞過去式，意為「應得的；理所當然的」。
vocabulary.example: Einstein received a well-deserved Nobel Prize for his contributions to physics.

vocabulary.definition: Cause something to change direction; turn aside.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞，意為「使偏斜；轉向；轉移（注意力或光線）」。故事中指引力使光線彎曲偏折。
vocabulary.example: Gravity can deflect light coming from distant stars.

vocabulary.definition: Having one's attention completely absorbed by something.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞，意為「全神貫注的；沉溺其中的」。形容專心致志到忽視周遭。
vocabulary.example: He was so engrossed in his physics equations that he forgot to eat lunch.

vocabulary.definition: Disorganized and incapable of serious, connected thought.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞，意為「注意力不集中的；心不在焉的；丟三落四的」。
vocabulary.example: Although brilliant, he seemed scatterbrained in his daily personal routine.

vocabulary.definition: Having or showing a habitual forgetfulness or inattention.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞，意為「心不在焉的；健忘的」。愛因斯坦經典的典型形象。
vocabulary.example: The absentminded professor used a bank check as a bookmark and lost it.

vocabulary.definition: In a state of peaceful happiness and satisfaction.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞，意為「心滿意足的；滿足的」。不追求奢華、對簡單生活感到滿意。
vocabulary.example: He was content with a simple sweater, his violin, and a sheet of paper.

vocabulary.definition: A comic performer who uses physical humor; a foolish person.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞/動詞，意為「小丑；愛開玩笑的人；扮小丑」。
vocabulary.example: He loved to stick out his tongue and clown around for photo journalists.

vocabulary.definition: Wrinkled, creased trousers made of thick ribbed cotton fabric.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語，意為「皺巴巴的燈心絨長褲」。描述愛因斯坦招牌的不修邊幅穿著風格。
vocabulary.example: He comfortably walked into the university wearing rumple corduroy pants.

vocabulary.definition: Unable to see distant objects clearly; myopic.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞，意為「近視的；缺乏遠見的」。看近清楚、看遠模糊的視力狀態。
vocabulary.example: Being nearsighted, he needed glasses to read the blackboard clearly.

vocabulary.definition: Having or showing a lack of common sense or seriousness; playful.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞，意為「傻氣的；滑稽可笑的；無聊的」。
vocabulary.example: He often made silly faces to make children laugh.

vocabulary.definition: A marine mammal producing loud, sharp vocal sounds.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語，意為「吠叫的海豹」。用於生動形容某種獨特洪亮叫聲或咳嗽聲。
vocabulary.example: The unique laugh of the professor sounded like a barking seal.

vocabulary.definition: Einstein enjoyed performing or showing off in front of audiences.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語（俚語 ham 意為愛表演/搶鏡頭的人），意為「愛因斯坦是個愛搶鏡頭、愛表演的人」。
vocabulary.example: Whenever cameras appeared, people realized that Einstein was a ham.

vocabulary.definition: The slow, deliberate movement of a beetle insect.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語，意為「甲蟲爬行」。用來比喻極其緩慢爬行或觀察甲蟲在彎曲表面移動的童年經歷。
vocabulary.example: He watched a beetle crawl on his blanket and wondered about space and movement.

vocabulary.definition: A remarkable fact or event that can be observed and studied.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「現象；罕見非凡的人事物」。科學界觀察到的自然現象。
vocabulary.example: Light bending around massive objects was a mind-boggling phenomenon.

vocabulary.definition: The art of making three-dimensional figures out of stone, wood, or metal.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞/動詞，意為「雕塑品；雕刻」。
vocabulary.example: Artists created a bronze sculpture to honor his scientific achievements.

vocabulary.definition: A dramatic work combining singing, orchestral music, and acting.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「歌劇」。愛因斯坦熱愛的古典音樂藝術形式之一。
vocabulary.example: In his free time, he enjoyed listening to classical opera and playing music.

vocabulary.definition: Declare one's public approval or support of; sign a document.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞，意為「代言；背書；公開支持；簽署」。
vocabulary.example: Companies offered him large sums of money to endorse their commercial products.

vocabulary.definition: A large or sufficient amount or quantity; abundance.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞/副詞/形容詞，意為「大量；充足；豐富」。
vocabulary.example: Don't worry, there is plenty of time to solve this physics puzzle.

vocabulary.definition: Removing one's clothing.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞/分詞，意為「脫衣服」。
vocabulary.example: He was so distracted that he started undressing for bed in the middle of the afternoon.

vocabulary.definition: Take off one's clothes.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞，意為「脫衣」。原形動詞。
vocabulary.example: He forgot where he was and began to undress right in his study.

vocabulary.definition: A fan who pursues famous people to get their signature.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語，意為「索取簽名的人；簽名迷」。跟著成名後的愛因斯坦到處跑的人群。
vocabulary.example: Everywhere he went, an autograph seeker would jump out with a pen.

vocabulary.definition: Harassed, pursued, or nagged persistently.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞過去式/形容詞，意為「被緊追不捨的；被纏得煩不勝煩的」。
vocabulary.example: The famous scientist was constantly hounded by curious reporters.

vocabulary.definition: A short documentary film of news events shown in theaters.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「新聞紀錄短片」。電視普及前在電影院播放的影像新聞紀錄。
vocabulary.example: People watched newsreel footage of the famous genius visiting America.

vocabulary.definition: A remarkable concurrence of events without apparent causal connection.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「巧合；偶然一致」。兩件無關的事同時發生。
vocabulary.example: It was a pure coincidence that both scientists published their ideas in the same year.

vocabulary.definition: An event where the moon passes between the sun and Earth, blocking sunlight.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語，意為「日食；日全蝕」。證實廣義相對論關鍵的天文現象。
vocabulary.example: Scientists photographed the solar eclipse of 1919 to test Einstein's theory.

vocabulary.definition: Mad, eccentric, or foolish (informal).
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞（口語），意為「古怪瘋狂的；古里古怪的」。
vocabulary.example: Some teachers mistakenly thought his unconventional ideas were completely nutty.

vocabulary.definition: An eccentric or foolish person with bizarre ideas.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞/形容詞（口語），意為「怪人；狂人；想法荒謬異想天開的人」。
vocabulary.example: Critics initially dismissed his bold relativity paper as the work of a crackpot.

vocabulary.definition: Propose formally for a award, honor, or official position.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞，意為「提名；推薦」。官方推薦角逐獎項。
vocabulary.example: Colleagues voted to nominate him for the Nobel Prize in Physics.

vocabulary.definition: Causing someone to feel ashamed, embarrassed, or foolish.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞，意為「令人羞辱的；使人難堪的」。極度令人丟臉的場合。
vocabulary.example: Failing the entrance exam on his first try was a humiliating experience.

vocabulary.definition: Form a circle around; surround completely.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞，意為「環繞；圍繞；圈住」。把事物包圍一圈。
vocabulary.example: The equator is an imaginary line that can encircle the Earth.

vocabulary.definition: An imaginary line drawn around the earth equally distant from both poles.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「赤道」。劃分地球南北半球的虛構緯線。
vocabulary.example: If you travel along the equator, you stay in the tropical zone.

vocabulary.definition: Thought of or produced a new thought or solution.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語（過去式），意為「想出了一個點子／靈感」。頭腦中萌生新構想。
vocabulary.example: While riding his bicycle, he came up with an idea that changed physics forever.

vocabulary.definition: Hold firmly; comprehend or understand fully.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞/名詞，意為「抓住；理解；領悟」。理解複雜艱深的理論。
vocabulary.example: It took years for other scientists to fully grasp his theory of relativity.

vocabulary.definition: A group of atoms bonded together, representing the smallest unit of a chemical compound.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「分子」。由原子組成的微觀物質基本單位。
vocabulary.example: Water is made of molecules containing hydrogen and oxygen.

vocabulary.definition: The basic unit of a chemical element.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「原子」。構成化學元素的微觀基本粒子。
vocabulary.example: Einstein proved the existence of atoms mathematically.

vocabulary.definition: Take off vertically from a launchpad (as a rocket).
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞短語，意為「（火箭）升空；發射點火起飛」。描述航天器快速發射。
vocabulary.example: Spacecraft use immense energy to blast off into outer space.

vocabulary.definition: Catch or enclose in a place; a device for catching animals.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞/名詞，意為「陷阱；困住；捕獲」。強大的引力連光都能捕捉困住。
vocabulary.example: A black hole's gravity is so strong that it can trap light.

vocabulary.definition: The force that attracts a body toward the center of the earth or another heavy object.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「地心引力；重力」。萬有引力。
vocabulary.example: He explained gravity not as a force, but as the bending of space-time.

vocabulary.definition: Completely fill to overflowing; study intensively in a short time.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞，意為「塞滿；臨時抱佛腳死記硬背」。考試前死記硬背資料。
vocabulary.example: He hated having to cram facts for school exams just to pass.

vocabulary.definition: Feet covered in perspiration.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語，意為「容易出汗的雙腳／流汗的腳」。愛因斯坦討厭穿襪子的原因之一。
vocabulary.example: He stopped wearing socks because he complained they got sweaty feet wet.

vocabulary.definition: Gnarled, enlarged veins, most commonly appearing in the legs.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語，意為「靜脈曲張」。腿部常見的血管腫脹膨大疾病。
vocabulary.example: Standing for long hours at a chalkboard can aggravate varicose veins.

vocabulary.definition: Intense, sharp, and deep brown eyes that seem to look right through someone.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語，意為「深邃銳利的棕色雙眼」。形容目光睿智銳利透徹。
vocabulary.example: He stared out at the universe with his piercing brown eyes.

vocabulary.definition: Hair that has gentle curves and forms natural S-shapes.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語，意為「捲曲的頭髮；波浪髮」。愛因斯坦招牌炸開蓬鬆的捲髮。
vocabulary.example: His wild wavy hair stuck out in all directions.

vocabulary.definition: A violent shattering or blowing apart with a loud noise; sudden outburst.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「爆炸；爆發；突發事件」。核能或原子彈的巨大爆炸能量。
vocabulary.example: The equation E=mc² showed how much energy an atomic explosion produces.

vocabulary.definition: A certificate awarded by an educational institution to show completion of study.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「畢業證書；文憑」。畢業獲得的學位證書。
vocabulary.example: He eventually finished high school in Switzerland and earned his diploma.

vocabulary.definition: The sport or activity of navigating a sailboat.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「航海；駕帆船」。愛因斯坦最喜愛的放鬆休閒運動。
vocabulary.example: He loved going sailing on quiet lakes, even though he didn't know how to swim.

vocabulary.definition: Strongly attracted and interested; spellbound.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞，意為「著迷的；深深被吸引的」。對事物抱有極大的好奇心。
vocabulary.example: Young Albert was fascinated by the magnetic compass his father gave him.

vocabulary.definition: A foolish, unstylish, or socially awkward person; an overly intellectual fan.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞（口語），意為「書呆子；科技控；沉迷學問的人」。
vocabulary.example: Before he became famous, some kids called him a quiet nerd.

vocabulary.definition: Giving food particles to birds in public parks.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語，意為「餵鴿子」。描繪晚年悠閒生活散步的場景。
vocabulary.example: In his later years in Princeton, he enjoyed sitting on park benches feeding pigeons.

vocabulary.definition: A female domestic servant.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「女傭；打掃女侍」。家庭打掃幫傭。
vocabulary.example: The house maid helped keep the messy study somewhat organized.

vocabulary.definition: A private teacher, typically one who teaches a single student or small group.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞/動詞，意為「家庭教師；私人導師」。輔導課業的教師。
vocabulary.example: A medical student worked as a tutor to teach Albert advanced mathematics.

vocabulary.definition: Uncontrolled outbursts of anger and frustration, typically in a young child.
vocabulary.analysis: 短語，意為「發脾氣；耍態度暴怒」。幼年情緒失控砸物品。
vocabulary.example: As a young child, Albert had severe temper tantrums and threw things at his sister.

vocabulary.definition: A person who does not eat meat or fish.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞/形容詞，意為「素食者；素食的」。不吃肉類的飲食習慣。
vocabulary.example: Later in life, he decided to become a strict vegetarian for health and moral reasons.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to or associated with Jews or Judaism.
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞，意為「猶太人的；猶太教的」。民族與宗教背景。
vocabulary.example: Because he was Jewish, he had to leave Germany when the Nazi party rose to power.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner unaffected by gravity; floating effortlessly.
vocabulary.analysis: 副詞，意為「無重力地；失重地；輕飄飄地」。形容失重狀態下的懸浮。
vocabulary.example: In a free-falling elevator, a person would float weightlessly.

vocabulary.definition: An event in which people compete for a prize; dispute.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞/動詞，意為「競賽；比賽；爭奪」。角逐勝負的活動。
vocabulary.example: He entered a mathematics contest and easily solved every puzzle.

vocabulary.definition: Give or grant as an official payment, prize, or reward.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞/動詞，意為「獎項；頒發；授予」。官方頒發榮譽。
vocabulary.example: The committee decided to award him the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics.

vocabulary.definition: Einstein's theory concerning space, time, and gravity.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「相對論」。愛因斯坦最出名的物理學巨作。
vocabulary.example: The General Theory of Relativity revolutionized how we view space and time.

vocabulary.definition: Change something radically or fundamentally.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞，意為「徹底改革；顛覆；給…帶來革命性變化」。徹底改寫歷史領域。
vocabulary.example: His famous equations helped revolutionize modern science.

vocabulary.definition: The scientific study of plants.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「植物學」。研究植物結構與生的科學。
vocabulary.example: While he excelled in physics, he showed little interest in botany.

vocabulary.definition: The scientific study of the behavior, structure, and classification of animals.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「動物學」。研究動物生命與行為的科學。
vocabulary.example: Zoology deals with animal life, whereas Einstein focused on physical forces.

vocabulary.definition: Fail an exam, course, or test (informal).
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞（口語），意為「不及格；考砸；當掉」。考試未達到通過標準。
vocabulary.example: He did not flunk math, contrary to popular urban legends.

vocabulary.definition: You are crazy, irrational, or foolish (informal phrase).
vocabulary.analysis: 短語（口語），意為「你瘋了；你真神經／不可理喻」。形容極度瘋狂異想天開。
vocabulary.example: When he told people time could slow down, they replied, 'You're nuts!'

vocabulary.definition: Expressing something clearly or formally.
vocabulary.analysis: 動詞/分詞，意為「陳述；明言；發表說明」。明確發言發表理論。
vocabulary.example: He published a paper stating that light travels in tiny energy quanta.

vocabulary.definition: The branch of mathematics concerned with the properties and relations of points, lines, and shapes.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「幾何學」。愛因斯坦少年時期深深著迷的數學分支。
vocabulary.example: At age twelve, Albert taught himself Euclidean geometry over one summer.

vocabulary.definition: Foolish or stupid; slow-witted (informal).
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞（口語），意為「傻乎乎的；反應遲鈍笨拙的」。
vocabulary.example: Because he spoke slowly as a child, some thought he was dopey.

vocabulary.definition: A stupid person; a mannequin or model.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞（口語），意為「笨蛋；傻瓜；木頭人」。
vocabulary.example: Strict teachers unfairly labeled young Albert a dummy.

vocabulary.definition: The branch of mathematics in which symbols and letters are used to represent numbers.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞，意為「代數學」。用符號運算數字的數學分支。
vocabulary.example: His uncle introduced him to algebra, calling it a game where you hunt for 'X'.

vocabulary.definition: Mad; crazy; eccentric (informal).
vocabulary.analysis: 形容詞/名詞（口語），意為「瘋瘋癲癲的；怪裡怪氣的；布谷鳥」。
vocabulary.example: Some of his radical physics ideas sounded cuckoo to traditional professors.

vocabulary.definition: A stupid or foolish person (informal); slang for cool or drugs.
vocabulary.analysis: 名詞（口語），意為「笨蛋；傻瓜（書名所指）」。書標題用詞，反諷大眾以為他是笨蛋。
vocabulary.example: The book humorously asks: Was Albert Einstein really a dope?
